title: Polls are rigged by money, bass poll winners
summary: Sam says polls can be won by money and names bassists like Niels-Henning Orsted Pedersen and George Mraz overlooked.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Let me ask you something about your feeling, we got into a thing talking about the writers and everything. And we talked about aspects of the kind of life, the kind of racism that has very much been a part of the society. What about the polls and the whole thing about polls?

Oh yeah, man. I'm glad you asked me that man. I'm glad you asked me that. Now I found out, now I know and you know that some of the guys that won polls shouldn't have. But I also found out that if you've got a few bucks, you can win those polls, man. And I think it's a darn man because I've heard a certain musician that plays the instrument that you and I play winning the polls quite frequently, man. And I know damn well that this man cannot play the bass like some of my friends can play the bass. He cannot play the bass like me or Hennings.
Yeah, Niels-Henning from Denmark. You were saying,
Yeah, now that is really a conspiracy with the polls, not only in bass players. I just used that as an example, you know.

A whole lot of - I've seen piano players that had a one to four. Now you know yourself that you've heard, played with people that were fantastic. Many of your people that you have on your staff at the school, man. I think this man is one of the most fantastic pianists I've heard.

So what are you going to do about people like Niels-Hennings, man? What are you going to do about George Mraz? People that can do it all. Even you yourself, you know. I haven't won the poll since 1960. How many years is that?
